newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Flurry of shipments underpin Vietnam rice market.
newsitem.headline: Flurry of shipments underpin Vietnam rice market.

text.p: Strong demand from abroad has underpinned Vietnamese rice prices in the past week, with shipments being lined up for Iran, Iraq, African countries and China, traders said on Thursday.
They said five percent broken grade was trading at around $280-285 a tonne FOB Saigon port. Ten percent broken was quoted at $265-270 a tonne.
"The market is firm because the harvest has finished and now the vessels are lining up in Saigon," said one trader.
He said 15 vessels were now waiting or loading in Saigon port and estimated that exports of Vietnamese rice this month would total around 300,000 tonnes.
China, whose southern rice crops were partially damaged by recent flooding, was expected to take about 20,000 tonnes of low grade rice from Vietnam this month.

Traders said Sri Lanka had invited tenders for 37,000 tonnes of 25 percent broken Vietnamese rice for delivery from the end of October to the end of November. One trader, who expected the tender result would be announced by the end of the week, said the lowest tender price was $238.50 a tonne.
Recent flooding in northern and central Vietnam, which inundated extensive areas of paddy, has not affected the market because harvesting had already ended when it came, traders said.
